title: Uncovering and Exploiting AMD Speculative Memory Access Predictors for Fun and Profit
problem: AMD processors contain Predictive Store Forwarding Predictor (PSFP) and Speculative Store Bypass Predictor (SSBP) that lack isolation mechanisms, allowing these predictors to be manipulated during transient execution to leak secrets across security domains.
motivation: Understanding speculative memory access predictor vulnerabilities is critical for developing effective mitigations and securing modern processor designs against transient execution attacks.
method: Reverse engineering uncovers PSFP and SSBP internal structures and state machines. The authors empirically demonstrate deliberate manipulation of these predictors during transient execution causing cross-domain secret leakage. Novel attacks are proposed: an out-of-place Spectre-STL variant and a new Spectre-CTL attack. Speculative Store Bypass Disable mitigation is validated to eliminate the vulnerabilities.
key_novelty: Discovery of two previously unknown speculative memory access predictors (PSFP and SSBP) and development of new Spectre-CTL attack variant exploiting these prediction mechanisms.
contributions: Reverse engineering and characterization of PSFP and SSBP predictors with internal structures and state machine designs
Empirical demonstration of predictor manipulation during transient execution enabling cross-domain secret leakage
Novel attacks including Spectre-STL variant and entirely new Spectre-CTL attack exploiting these predictors
Validation that Speculative Store Bypass Disable mitigates vulnerabilities with measured performance overhead
limitations: Paper does not discuss applicability to other processor vendors or analyze alternative mitigation strategies beyond SSBD.
